data.description:
Turn the planning artifacts into a committed repository that every later task branches from. This is the only task that commits directly on master.

Why: the repo has zero commits. Branch-per-task (docs/SPEC.md §2) needs a base. Everything after this task is a feature branch merged with --no-ff.

Scope:
- Root .gitignore (Go, Node, *.db, .DS_Store, .env, dist/, plus the .lattice/.gitignore'd runtime paths are already handled inside .lattice/).
- .editorconfig (2-space for ts/json/yaml/md, tabs for go, LF, final newline).
- Move sample_listings.json to data/sample_listings.json (SPEC §3). Nothing else references it yet.
- Create backend/ and frontend/ as empty directories with a .gitkeep each, and docs/ (already has SPEC.md).
- Makefile skeleton with phony targets up, down, dev-api, dev-web, test, lint, check, smoke, dist. Targets that have nothing to run yet print "not yet implemented" and exit 1 so make check fails loudly until BC-2/BC-7 fill them in.
- README.md with the project name "Brillio Listings", one paragraph on what it is, and a "Status: scaffolding" line. BC-15 writes the real README.
- Commit everything present (CLAUDE.md, agents.md, BRANDING.md, docs/, data/, the two PDFs, .lattice/ board state) as the initial commit on master with message "chore: bootstrap repository". No emoji in the message (BRANDING.md §8).

Out of scope: any Go or TypeScript code, Docker files, CI.

Acceptance:
- git log shows exactly one commit on master containing the files above.
- git status is clean afterward.
- make check exits non-zero with a clear "not yet implemented" message.
- data/sample_listings.json exists and the root copy is gone.

Validation: N/A (no running system); record a one-line justification with --role validation.
data.title: Repo bootstrap: initial commit, layout, Makefile, tooling baseline

data.description:
Stand up the Go service skeleton that BC-3, BC-4 and BC-5 build inside. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §2, §3, §5.1, §5.5 (envelope), §5.6, §11.

Why: every backend task needs the module, the router, the middleware chain and the shared domain types to exist first. Defining the shared types here lets BC-3 (domain logic) and BC-4 (store) run in parallel.

Scope:
- backend/go.mod, module path `brillio/backend`, `go 1.27`. Stdlib only.
- cmd/api/main.go: load config, build router, http.Server with Read/Write/Idle timeouts, graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM honoring SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, slog JSON logger to stdout at LOG_LEVEL.
- internal/config: parse §11 env vars with defaults; invalid LOG_LEVEL or SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT is a startup error.
- internal/domain: types only. `Listing` per §4, `ListingStatus` with constants and `ParseStatus`, `SearchFilter{MinPrice, MaxPrice *float64; MinBedrooms *int; City, Keyword string; KeywordTokens []string; Statuses []ListingStatus}`. No logic.
- internal/httpapi: `NewRouter(deps Deps) http.Handler` using Go 1.22 ServeMux patterns. Middleware in order: request ID (echo X-Request-ID or generate 16 random bytes hex), request log line (method, path, status, duration, request id, remote addr), panic recovery to a 500 envelope, CORS per §5.6. JSON helpers `writeJSON` and `writeError` producing the §5.5 envelope. 404 and 405 handlers that return the envelope. GET /healthz returning {"status":"ok"} (DB ping arrives with BC-4; leave a `Pinger` interface in Deps that may be nil).
- backend/.golangci.yml: default linters plus errcheck, govet, staticcheck, revive.
- Root Makefile: fill in dev-api (go run ./cmd/api), and the backend halves of test (go test -race ./...), lint (golangci-lint run), check.
- Tests: config table; middleware (request id echoed and generated, panic becomes 500 envelope with no stack in body, CORS preflight 204 with the right headers, unknown route 404 envelope, wrong method 405 envelope).

Out of scope: SQLite, the search handler, OpenAPI, Docker.

Acceptance:
- `go run ./cmd/api` serves GET /healthz 200 with Content-Type application/json and an X-Request-ID header.
- `make lint` and `make test` pass for the backend.
- SIGTERM produces a "shutting down" log line and exit code 0.
- internal/domain compiles with the shared types and zero logic.

Validation: run the binary, curl /healthz with and without an X-Request-ID header, send SIGTERM, paste the output as evidence with --role validation.
data.title: Backend scaffold: Go 1.27 HTTP server with health, slog, request IDs, CORS, graceful shutdown, config, lint

data.description:
Implement the ranking core as pure Go with no I/O: budget fit, recency, score, deterministic ordering, pagination with global ranks. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §6.2, §6.3, §6.4, §8 (domain list). Clock is injected; never call time.Now() in this package.

Why: this is the logic the interviewer will probe hardest ("why this formula?"). It must be small, readable and exhaustively tested, and it must not depend on the store (BC-4) so both can land in parallel.

Scope (package internal/domain, building on the types from BC-2):
- Exported constants `BudgetWeight = 0.6`, `RecencyWeight = 0.4`, `RecencyHalfLifeDays = 30`.
- `BudgetFit(price, target float64) float64` asymmetric per §6.2 (under: price/target; over: max(0, 1 - 2*pctOver)).
- `AgeDays(listedDate, now time.Time) int` whole calendar days in UTC, clamped at 0 for future dates.
- `Recency(listedDate, now time.Time) float64` = 0.5^(ageDays/30).
- `Score(budgetFit *float64, recency float64) float64`: with budget 0.6*fit + 0.4*recency; without budget, recency alone.
- `Rank(listings []Listing, in RankInput) []Scored` where `RankInput{TargetBudget *float64; Now time.Time}` and `Scored{Listing; Relevance{Score float64; BudgetFit *float64; Recency float64}}`. Sort per §6.3 on unrounded score desc, then listedDate desc, price asc, source asc, id asc. Use slices.SortStableFunc.
- `Paginate(ranked []Scored, page, pageSize int) (Page, error)` returning `Page{Items []RankedItem; Page, PageSize, TotalItems, TotalPages int}` where RankedItem adds `Rank int` = 1-based index in the whole set. Invalid page (<1) or pageSize (outside 1..100) returns a typed error the handler can map to §5.5 codes; page past end returns an empty Items with correct metadata.
- Full precision kept here; rounding to four decimals is the handler's job (BC-5).
- Tests, table-driven, per §8: worked values from §6.2 (450000/405000/495000/562500/675000; ages 0/30/60/90), asymmetry at equal percentages, future dates, no budget, tied scores with the exact tiebreak order asserted on a crafted fixture, no matches, every pagination boundary including rank continuity across pages (page 2 of pageSize 10 starts at 11), pageSize 1 and 100, zero items giving totalPages 0.

Acceptance:
- `go test -race ./internal/domain/...` green with every §8 domain case present by name.
- Package imports nothing outside the standard library.
- golangci-lint clean.
- A short doc comment at the top of scoring.go states the formula in words; BC-15 will quote it.

Validation: N/A (pure library, no running surface). Record a one-line justification with --role validation and cite the test output.
data.title: Domain: relevance scoring, deterministic ordering, pagination with ranks (pure Go)

data.description:
SQLite persistence: open, migrate, seed from JSON, filtered search query, cities query, ping. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §4.1, §4.2, §5.2, §6.1, §8 (store list), §11.

Why: the handout wants real logic over the dataset; SQLite gives a real WHERE clause (filters) while ranking stays in Go (BC-3). Seeding must be idempotent because the container restarts on every hot reload.

Scope (package internal/store, plus seed loading):
- `Open(ctx, dsn string) (*Store, error)` using modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go). Pragmas: busy_timeout=5000, foreign_keys=on, journal_mode=WAL when not :memory:. Single connection for :memory: so the schema is shared.
- Embedded migrations under internal/store/migrations/ (0001_listings.sql per §4.1 including schema_migrations and the four indexes). `Migrate(ctx)` applies pending files in order inside a transaction; running it twice is a no-op.
- `seed.Load(path string) ([]domain.Listing, error)`: strict JSON decode (DisallowUnknownFields), per-record validation and normalization per §4.2; errors name the record index and field. `(*Store).Upsert(ctx, []domain.Listing) (int, error)` in one transaction with ON CONFLICT(source, id) DO UPDATE.
- `(*Store).Search(ctx, domain.SearchFilter) ([]domain.Listing, error)`: builds the WHERE clause per §6.1 with parameterized args only; keyword tokens use `instr(lower(description), ?) > 0`; status uses IN with one placeholder per value; ORDER BY source, id.
- `(*Store).Cities(ctx) ([]string, error)` distinct case-insensitively, sorted, first-seen casing.
- `(*Store).Ping(ctx) error`; wire into main.go so /healthz returns 503 {"status":"degraded"} when it fails. main.go opens the store, migrates, seeds from LISTINGS_FILE, and exits non-zero with a clear log on any failure.
- Tests per §8 store list against :memory: using the real data/sample_listings.json: 12 rows after seed, 12 after seeding twice, each filter alone and combined, keyword tokens containing % and _ are literal, multi-token AND, status sets, city case-insensitive and trimmed, Cities output exact.

Acceptance:
- `go run ./cmd/api` against a fresh DB_PATH logs "seeded 12 listings" and /healthz is ok.
- Every filter in §6.1 has a passing test; `make check` green for the backend.
- No string concatenation of user input into SQL anywhere (reviewer greps for it).

Validation: start the binary with DB_PATH=/tmp/x.db, confirm 12 rows (sqlite3 CLI or a one-off go run), curl /healthz, restart and confirm still 12; attach the output with --role validation.
data.title: SQLite store: schema migrations, JSON seed loader, filtered search query, cities query

data.description:
The search endpoint end to end: strict query parsing, collected validation errors with field codes, the pipeline in one readable function, response mapping, plus the cities endpoint. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §5.2, §5.3, §5.4, §5.5, §6, §8 (httpapi list). Messages for field errors come from BRANDING.md §7.2 where a string exists.

Why: this is where "handle invalid input deliberately" is demonstrated. Unknown params are rejected, all problems are returned together, a page past the end is a 200, and a city with no matches is a 200. The pipeline function is the thing the interviewer reads when adding a requirement, so it must show its stages plainly.

Scope (package internal/httpapi):
- query.go: `ParseSearchQuery(url.Values) (SearchQuery, []FieldError)`. Allowlist of param names; anything else yields `unknown_param`. Empty value = absent. Numbers via strconv.ParseFloat; integers must be whole (`not_an_integer`). Rules and codes per §5.3/§5.5: negative, not_positive, out_of_range (pageSize 1..100, page >= 1), too_long (city 100, keyword 200), invalid_enum (status), min_gt_max reported once on maxPrice. Keyword split on whitespace into lowercase tokens. Status accepts repeats and comma-separated values; absent means all three. Defaults page 1, pageSize 10.
- search.go: handler for GET /api/listings/search implementing §6 in one function with a comment marking the dedupe slot. Dependencies: a Searcher interface (BC-4 store), a `Now func() time.Time` (main injects time.Now, tests inject a fixed clock). Maps domain output to the §5.4 JSON: rank, relevance rounded to four decimals, budgetFit null without budget, scoring block (weights 0/1 without budget, asOf = now UTC YYYY-MM-DD), appliedFilters with nulls.
- cities.go: GET /api/cities per §5.2.
- Tests per §8 httpapi list with httptest and a seeded :memory: store: every rule returns 400 with the right code and all errors collected; unknown param; page past end is 200 with empty items and correct metadata; empty city is 200 with totalItems 0; happy path for targetBudget=450000&city=Springfield with a fixed clock asserts rank order and the exact relevance numbers computed from §6.2; status filter; keyword with %; X-Request-ID present on every response.

Acceptance:
- Response bodies match §5.4 and §5.5 field for field (a test unmarshals into a struct with DisallowUnknownFields both ways).
- `make check` green.
- The pipeline function reads top to bottom as parse, search, [dedupe slot], rank, paginate, respond.

Validation: against the running API, curl the §10 smoke queries plus status=pending, keyword=%25 (encoded percent), pageSize=0, and minprice=1 (lowercase typo); paste the responses with --role validation.
data.title: Search API: strict query parsing, validation with field codes, pipeline handler, cities endpoint

data.description:
Write the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the API and serve it from the binary. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §5.7 and §5.1–5.6.

Why: senior bar. It also gives the interviewer a precise contract to read, and the sync test keeps the handler's param allowlist and the document from drifting.

Scope:
- backend/openapi.yaml, OpenAPI 3.1: paths /healthz, /api/cities, /api/listings/search, /api/openapi.yaml. Components: Listing, ListingResult (with rank and relevance), PageMeta, ScoringMeta, SearchResponse, ErrorEnvelope, FieldError with the code enum from §5.5. Every query param with type, constraints, default and a one-line description; document the unknown-parameter rule and the page-past-end and empty-city behavior in the operation description. Examples lifted from §5.4 and §5.5.
- Embed with embed.FS and serve at GET /api/openapi.yaml with Content-Type application/yaml.
- Tests: handler returns 200 and the body parses as YAML; a sync test that reads the allowlist of param names from the search handler and asserts each appears under the search operation's parameters, and vice versa.
- Run one external validator once (for example `npx @redocly/cli lint backend/openapi.yaml`) and record its output in a task comment; do not add it to make check.

Acceptance:
- curl /api/openapi.yaml returns the document.
- Validator reports no errors.
- Sync test green; `make check` green.

Validation: the curl and the validator output, attached with --role validation.
data.title: OpenAPI 3.1 document, embedded and served at /api/openapi.yaml, with param sync test

data.description:
Create the frontend project with the exact toolchain, the design tokens, the fonts, the pinned app shell and the Header. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §2, §3, §7.6, §10 (proxy). Design: BRANDING.md §2.1 (tokens), §2.5, §3.1 (fonts), §3.2 (scale), §4 (grid, shell, breakpoints), §5.1 (Header). Reference rendering: docs/branding-demo.html.

Why: every component task (BC-9, BC-10, BC-11) needs tokens, the type scale and the test harness in place, and the shell grid is what makes "app, not document" true.

Scope:
- `npm create vite@latest frontend -- --template react-ts`, then pin latest stable: React 19, Vite 8, TypeScript 7, Vitest 5, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/user-event, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom, typescript-eslint, eslint-plugin-react-hooks, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, prettier. No other runtime or dev dependencies.
- tsconfig strict plus noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes. ESLint flat config. .prettierrc. vitest config with jsdom and src/test/setup.ts (jest-dom matchers).
- vite.config.ts: proxy /api and /healthz to VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET, default http://localhost:8080.
- index.html: `<title>Brillio Listings</title>`, the BRANDING §3.1 Google Fonts link, lang="en".
- src/styles/tokens.css: the §2.1 :root block verbatim, plus `--font-display`, `--font-ui`, the §3.2 sizes/leading as custom properties, spacing (8px grid, 24/16px gutters, 1040px content width, 760px breakpoint noted in a comment since media queries cannot read custom properties).
- src/styles/global.css: html/body height 100% and overflow hidden, paper background, ink text, Figtree body at 15/22, `font-optical-sizing: auto`, `color-scheme: light`, a `.tabular` utility, reset for buttons/inputs to inherit font.
- src/styles/shell.module.css: §4.2 grid with rows `auto auto auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto`, results region `overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain`, 1040px centered content, gutters per §4.1.
- src/components/Header: wordmark BRILLIO LISTINGS per §3.2 (Figtree 13/600, +0.16em, uppercase), optional scope label at right in ink-2, 56px tall, hairline below. Test: renders wordmark and optional scope.
- App.tsx renders the shell with Header and placeholder regions labelled by role.
- Makefile: dev-web (npm run dev), frontend halves of test, lint (eslint + tsc --noEmit + prettier --check), check.

Acceptance:
- `npm run dev` shows the header on paper ground with the fonts loaded (check computed font-family in devtools).
- `npm run build`, `npm test`, and `make lint` all pass.
- package.json contains only the listed dependencies.
- No emoji anywhere (BRANDING §8).

Validation: open http://localhost:5173 in a browser (c11-browser skill), confirm the header renders and the document itself does not scroll; attach a screenshot with --role validation.
data.title: Frontend scaffold: Vite 8 + React 19 + TS 7, lint, Vitest/RTL, API proxy, BRANDING tokens, app shell, Header

data.description:
The frontend's non-visual core: API types and client, URL state hook, search hook with abort and previous-results memory, cities hook, and the BRANDING formatters. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §7.1, §7.2, §7.3, §8 (frontend hooks and formatters). Design: BRANDING.md §7.1 formatting table.

Why: components (BC-9, BC-10, BC-11) must be pure props-in renderers; everything stateful and every string-formatting rule lives here with its own tests, so three component tasks can run in parallel.

Scope:
- src/api/types.ts exactly as §7.3. src/api/errors.ts with ApiError union and a `parseErrorResponse(res)` helper. src/api/client.ts: `searchListings(params, signal?)` builds the query string (undefined omitted, status repeated, numbers as plain strings), `getCities(signal?)`; non-2xx bodies parse into ApiError; fetch TypeError and AbortError map to kind 'network' (the hook ignores aborts).
- src/hooks/useSearchParamsState.ts per §7.1: parse window.location.search into SearchParams on mount (numbers parsed, invalid values dropped), `setSearch(next)` pushes the new query string without page, `setPage(n)` pushes with only page changed, `clear()` pushes an empty query, popstate re-reads; pageSize preserved if present.
- src/hooks/useListingSearch.ts per §7.2 returning SearchState; AbortController per request; previous data retained during loading and on invalid/error; the state 'empty' when totalItems is 0; 'invalid' for validation errors.
- src/hooks/useCities.ts: load once, return string[] (empty on failure, error to console.error).
- src/format/money.ts, date.ts, listing.ts implementing every row of BRANDING §7.1: price `$450,000`; `2 bd`; `1 ba` / `1.5 ba`; `1,450 sqft`; `Listed Aug 29` with `, YYYY` when not the current year (year injected for tests); source `MLS_A` to `MLS A`; status label uppercase only when not active; score two decimals; rank `No. 1`; `1 result` / `12 results`; `Page 1 of 2`; monogram initials `Sp`.
- Tests per §8: client query building and error parsing (400 validation with fields, 500 http, TypeError network, abort ignored); both hooks under jsdom with history and popstate; every formatter row.

Acceptance:
- All tests green; `make lint` green.
- No new runtime dependencies.
- Types compile against a fixture built from the real sample data (src/test/fixtures.ts with three listings and one full SearchResponse).

Validation: N/A until BC-12 wires a page. Record a one-line justification with --role validation and cite the test output.
data.title: Frontend core: API client and types, URL state and search hooks, BRANDING formatters

data.description:
The FilterBar: seven fields with the BRANDING field anatomy, client-side validation using the exact copy, server error mapping, Search and Clear. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §7.4 (FilterBar), §5.5 (codes). Design: BRANDING.md §5.2 (fields and states), §5.8 (buttons), §5.9 (invalid input row), §7.2 (strings), §4.4 (breakpoints), §3.2 (Label, Body, Button). Reference: docs/branding-demo.html.

Why: this is the "real inputs" deliverable and where invalid input is caught before it is sent. The Status field is the one addition beyond the brief (engineering interview decision, SPEC §13.1) and must follow §5.2's seventh-field rule exactly.

Scope (src/components/FilterBar, props per SPEC §7.4):
- Fields in order: Min price, Max price, Min bedrooms, City (select, "Any" first, options from the cities prop), Keyword, Target budget, Status (select: Any / Active / Pending / Sold). Labels and placeholders verbatim from §7.2.
- Anatomy: label above (Label style), value (Body 15), 1px ink-2 underline; focus 2px oxblood underline and no ring; invalid 2px oxblood underline with the message beneath in oxblood Meta 13; disabled ink-3 with line underline. Select shows the ▾ glyph in ink-2.
- Local draft state seeded from the `value` prop and re-seeded when it changes (URL navigation). Price and budget inputs show digits while typing and `$400,000` on blur (formatters from BC-8); min bedrooms step 1.
- Client-side rules with exact strings: `Min price must be less than max price.` (marks both price fields, message under Max price), `Min bedrooms must be 0 or more.`, `Target budget must be more than $0.`; negative prices use the same voice. Search disabled while invalid or while `loading`.
- Server errors: map `serverErrors` by field and code onto the same marks; `min_gt_max` marks both and shows under Max price; unmapped fields fall through to a single line under the bar.
- Search is the one primary button (§5.8), Clear a text button. Enter in any field submits. `onSearch` receives a SearchParams with numbers parsed, empty values omitted, status omitted when Any.
- Layout per §4.4: one row above 760px (wrapping before any field drops below 130px), two columns at or below 760px with Search full width on its own row with Clear.
- Tests: labels and placeholders verbatim, blur formatting, each invalid rule and its placement, server error mapping including min_gt_max, submit payload shape, Clear, Enter submits, disabled while loading, aria-invalid and aria-describedby wiring.

Acceptance:
- Side by side with docs/branding-demo.html the bar is indistinguishable at both breakpoints (allowing for the added Status field).
- Tests green; no oxblood outside §2.2 jobs 1, 3 and 4; no icons, no emoji.

Validation: N/A until BC-12. Record a one-line justification with --role validation and cite the test output.
data.title: FilterBar: seven fields, client-side validation with exact copy, server error mapping, Search and Clear

data.description: The results surface: ListingCard with Monogram and ScorePill, ListingList, and the NoResults and ErrorState screens. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §7.4, §7.5, §7.6. Design: BRANDING.md §5.4 (card), §5.5 (monogram), §5.6 (score), §5.9 (no results, error), §3.2 (Price, Address, Meta, Description, State heading), §4.1, §4.4, §7.1, §7.2. Reference: docs/branding-demo.html. Why: the handout requires address, price, bedrooms and relevance score per result; BRANDING fixes exactly how. Keeping the card a pure renderer over ListingResult lets it be tested against the real sample data. Scope (props per SPEC §7.4): - ListingCard: three columns (monogram 72px, text, price block right-aligned); hairline above every card but the first (handled by ListingList). Text column: address in Bodoni 22 with `text-wrap: balance`, verbatim; meta line in Figtree 13 ink-2 with ` · ` separators in this order: status label only when not active, `City, ST ZIP`, bd, ba, sqft, `Listed Mon D`, source; description one line with ellipsis, each case-insensitive keyword match wrapped in weight 600 (never color). Price block: price in Bodoni 28/500 right-aligned over ScorePill. At or below 760px the price block moves under the meta line, left-aligned, price before rank (§4.4). No hover state, no link. - Monogram: 72×54 stone block, city initials (first upper, second lower) in Bodoni 26 ink-2, centered; never below 24px. - ScorePill: `No. N` pill (1px ink border, radius 999px, Figtree 11/500 +0.04em, padding 2px 8px) followed by the score to two decimals in Figtree 13 ink-2 tabular. - ListingList: renders cards separated by hairlines inside a region with a visually clear heading for focus management (BC-12 moves focus here), `aria-live="polite"`. - NoResults: centered 96px from the top: `No results.` (State heading, italic Bodoni 22), `Adjust your filters.` (Body ink-2), `Clear filters` text button calling onClear. - ErrorState: centered `Couldn't load results.` (State heading) and a `Try again` text button calling onRetry. No error code shown. - Tests using fixtures from BC-8 built on the real listings: every meta item renders in order; PENDING shows for A7 and nothing for active; keyword emphasis wraps `Pets`/`pets` case-insensitively and leaves the rest untouched; ScorePill text `No. 11` and `0.87`; Monogram `Sp`, `Vi`, `Fa`; NoResults and ErrorState strings verbatim and callbacks fire; no ``, no icons. Acceptance: - A card rendered from A1 matches the demo card pixel-for-pixel in structure and type (visual check against docs/branding-demo.html). - Tests green; lint green; no emoji; no oxblood anywhere in these components except the two text buttons. Validation: N/A until BC-12. Record a one-line justification with --role validation and cite the test output.
data.title: Results surface: ListingCard, Monogram, ScorePill, ListingList, NoResults, ErrorState

data.description:
Pager, StatusLine and LoadingLine: the three pinned chrome pieces around the results. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §7.4, §7.5, §7.6. Design: BRANDING.md §5.3 (status line), §5.7 (pager), §5.9 (loading row), §6 (motion), §2.2 jobs 2 and 5, §7.2 strings. Reference: docs/branding-demo.html.

Why: pagination must be visible and operable (handout), the status line is where "ranked for $450,000" tells the user what the ordering means, and the loading line is the only animation in the product.

Scope (props per SPEC §7.4):
- Pager: 48px, hairline above. `‹ Previous` left and `Next ›` right as text buttons; every page number centered with 16px gaps (the dataset is small; windowing is noted in docs/EXTENSIONS.md). Current page in oxblood weight 500 with a 1px oxblood underline and `aria-current="page"`. Disabled Previous/Next in ink-3 using the `disabled` attribute so they are not focusable. Glyphs are text, not icons. Hidden entirely when totalPages is 0.
- StatusLine: Meta 13 ink-2, two halves. Left derived from SearchState with the BC-8 formatters: `12 results · ranked for $450,000`, `12 results · newest first` when scoring.targetBudget is null, `1 result` singular, `Loading` while loading, `0 results` when empty, empty on error. Right: `Page 1 of 2`, empty when there are no pages.
- LoadingLine: 2px track in line color under the filter bar; when active a 40% oxblood segment slides left to right, 1.2s linear, looping; `role="progressbar"` with an accessible name; under prefers-reduced-motion a static full-width oxblood line (§6). Inactive renders the empty track so layout never shifts.
- Tests: every StatusLine string for every state (idle, loading with and without previous, success with and without budget, empty, invalid, error); singular/plural; Pager bounds and callbacks, aria-current, disabled ends not focusable, hidden at zero pages; LoadingLine active/inactive and the reduced-motion branch.

Acceptance:
- Strings match BRANDING §5.3 and §7.2 verbatim (tests assert exact text).
- Only oxblood uses are the pager text buttons, the current page and the loading segment.
- Tests and lint green; no emoji.

Validation: N/A until BC-12. Record a one-line justification with --role validation and cite the test output.
data.title: Pager, StatusLine and LoadingLine components

data.description:
Compose the whole page: the pinned shell, URL state, fetching, every state, the pager, keyword emphasis, focus management, and the integration tests. Then prove it against the real API. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §7.1–7.6, §8 (SearchPage list). Design: BRANDING.md §4.2 (shell), §5.9 (states), §1 ("App, not document").

Why: this is the "wired together end to end" deliverable. Everything before it is a part; this is the product. Its validation is the real end-to-end check for the frontend.

Scope:
- src/pages/SearchPage.tsx composes Header, FilterBar, LoadingLine, StatusLine, the results region (ListingList, NoResults or ErrorState), and Pager in the §4.2 grid from BC-7; the results region is the only scroller.
- Wiring: useSearchParamsState feeds useListingSearch; FilterBar `value` comes from the URL, `onSearch` pushes new params (page reset), `onClear` clears the URL, Pager `onChange` pushes page; keyword tokens for emphasis come from the URL state; `serverErrors` come from the 'invalid' state; Try again re-runs the last request; cities from useCities.
- Initial load with an empty URL performs a default search (all listings, newest first). After a page change move focus to the results heading. Keep previous results on screen while loading, on invalid input and on error, per §5.9.
- Remove the BC-7 placeholders; App.tsx renders SearchPage.
- Integration tests with stubbed fetch and the BC-8 fixtures: loading then success renders cards and status; loading then empty renders NoResults and `0 results`; a 400 with min_gt_max marks both price fields and keeps the previous list; a 500 and a network failure render ErrorState and Try again re-fetches; page change issues a new request with page=2, aborts the previous one, and the first card reads `No. 11`; popstate restores page 1; the default search fires on mount.

Acceptance:
- All §8 SearchPage tests green; `make check` green for both halves.
- With api and web running the full flow works in a real browser.

Validation (required, this is the frontend's e2e gate): run the API (native or compose) and the web app; in a browser via the c11-browser skill: (1) default load shows 12 results, newest first, `12 results · newest first`; (2) Target budget 450000 and City Springfield gives 4 results ranked with A1 as No. 1 and `ranked for $450,000`; (3) Min price 500000 and Max price 400000 marks both fields with the message under Max price and sends no request; (4) Keyword `pets` emphasizes matches in descriptions; (5) with pageSize=3 in the URL, page 2 shows No. 4 and the back button returns to page 1; (6) stop the API, search, see `Couldn't load results.`, start the API, Try again recovers; (7) the document never scrolls, only the results region. Attach screenshots or the browser transcript with --role validation.
data.title: SearchPage: compose shell, wire URL state and fetch, all states, pager; integration tests and browser e2e

data.description:
Docker Compose dev stack with hot reload for both halves, health-gated startup, and a smoke target. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §10, §11, §2 (versions).

Why: the owner asked for Docker Compose on the latest versions, and the interview addendum says the environment must be running on the laptop with no setup time lost. One command brings up a reloading stack; `make smoke` proves it in seconds.

Scope:
- backend/Dockerfile.dev: golang:1.27-alpine, CGO_ENABLED=0, installs air, workdir /app, module cache in a named volume. backend/.air.toml watching *.go and rebuilding ./cmd/api.
- Web service on node:24-alpine (a Dockerfile.dev only if a plain image command is not enough): bind-mount ./frontend, anonymous volume for node_modules, `npm ci && npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0`.
- compose.yaml per §10: api with env from §11 (DB_PATH=/data/listings.db, LISTINGS_FILE=/data/sample_listings.json, CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173), ./data bind-mounted, port 8080, healthcheck wget /healthz; web with VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET=http://api:8080, port 5173, depends_on api service_healthy.
- Makefile: up (docker compose up), down (docker compose down -v), smoke.
- scripts/smoke.sh: bring the stack up detached, wait for api health (bounded retries), GET /api/cities and assert it contains Springfield, GET /api/listings/search?targetBudget=450000&city=Springfield and assert items non-empty and the first rank is 1, GET with minPrice=5&maxPrice=1 and assert 400 and code min_gt_max, GET http://localhost:5173 and assert 200 with the title Brillio Listings, then tear down. Plain sh with curl and grep; no jq dependency.
- Confirm that saving a Go file restarts api inside the container and saving a TSX file hot-reloads the page.

Acceptance:
- From a clean checkout `docker compose up` reaches healthy api and a reachable web on :5173 that proxies to api.
- `make smoke` passes and exits 0; `make down` leaves no containers or volumes behind.
- Go and TSX edits reload without restarting compose.

Validation: run `make smoke` and paste the output; open http://localhost:5173 served by compose and perform one search in the browser; attach both with --role validation.
data.title: Docker Compose dev stack with hot reload, health gating, and make smoke

data.description:
Audit the running UI against BRANDING.md and the reference demo, and fix every deviation that is a frontend bug rather than a design change. Design: BRANDING.md in full, with special attention to §2.2 (the five oxblood jobs), §3.3 (type rules), §4 (shell and breakpoints), §5 (every component), §6 (motion), §7 (copy and formatting), §8 (don'ts). Reference: docs/branding-demo.html. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §13 for known engineering deltas.

Why: three component tasks and a wiring task were built in parallel by different agents; this pass is the one place the whole surface is checked as one system by fresh eyes before the README and packaging.

Scope:
- With api and web running, compare each component to the demo at a width above 760px and at or below 760px.
- Checklist, each recorded pass or fixed in a task comment: oxblood appears only in the five §2.2 jobs; no radius except the rank pill; no shadows, gradients, translucency, icons, images; Bodoni never below 18px; tabular figures where digits sit in columns; uppercase only in labels and the wordmark; every §7.2 string verbatim; every §7.1 format; the document never scrolls; pinned header, filter bar, status line and pager; loading line is the only animation and is static under reduced motion; disabled looks use ink-3 and stone, not opacity; keyboard-only pass through search, pagination and Try again; `grep -rP "[\x{1F300}-\x{1FAFF}\x{2600}-\x{27BF}]"` over the repo finds nothing.
- Fix small CSS, markup and copy deviations in place. Anything that would require changing BRANDING.md itself (for example the Status field row, SPEC §13.1) is not changed here: raise it with `lattice needs-human` naming the section.

Acceptance:
- A checklist comment on the task listing every BRANDING section with pass or fixed.
- Screenshots at both breakpoints for the default search, the no-results state, the invalid-input state and the error state, attached to the task.
- `make check` still green.

Validation: the screenshots and the keyboard pass are the evidence; attach with --role validation.
data.title: Branding conformance pass: audit UI against BRANDING.md and the demo, fix deviations

data.description:
Write the README the handout asks for: run instructions, architecture, the scoring approach and its trade-offs. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §1, §2, §6, §9, §12; handout "Deliverables". Voice: BRANDING.md §7 (plain product, sentence case, no emoji).

Why: the handout grades "a short README explaining your scoring approach and any trade-offs". The interviewer reads this before the code. Every claim must be true of the code as merged.

Scope (README.md, under roughly 250 lines):
- What it is: two sentences.
- Run it: `docker compose up` then http://localhost:5173; native alternative with `make dev-api` and `make dev-web`; `make check`; `make smoke`; required tools and versions.
- Project layout: the §3 tree, trimmed to what exists.
- API: the three endpoints with one curl example each and a pointer to /api/openapi.yaml; the error envelope in five lines.
- Scoring: the formula in words and symbols, the asymmetric budget fit and why (over budget hurts twice as much), the 30-day half-life and why, the 0.6/0.4 weights and why, tie-breaking, the worked example from §6.2, what happens without a budget (newest first), and where the constants live. Quote the doc comment from BC-3.
- Handling invalid input: strict unknown params, all errors collected, page past the end is a 200, an empty city is a 200, and why each.
- Trade-offs: SQL filters with Go ranking (and the scaling path), SQLite over a server database, keeping cross-source duplicates visible, stdlib only, no dark mode by decision.
- Extending it: three sentences and a link to docs/EXTENSIONS.md.
- Testing: what is covered in each half and how to run it.

Acceptance:
- Every command in the README runs as written (BC-17 proves it from the zip).
- Every number and formula matches internal/domain.
- No emoji; no exclamation marks.

Validation: N/A (documentation). Record a one-line justification with --role validation; BC-17 performs the fresh-directory check.
data.title: README: run instructions, architecture, scoring rationale and trade-offs

data.description:
Spike: write docs/EXTENSIONS.md, the playbook for the requirements the interviewer is likely to add live. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §9. Design hooks: BRANDING.md §5 ("where a new requirement goes" notes in each component) and §10.

Why: the live session is explicitly about extending a design already built, narrating the reasoning. A rehearsed playbook with the exact seams turns a surprise into a demo. This is also where the owner rehearses before the session.

Scope (docs/EXTENSIONS.md):
- One entry per §9 item: the requirement in one line; the exact files and functions to touch (verified to exist by grep at writing time); the API change (params, response fields) and the UI change (which BRANDING §5 slot); the tests to add; a minutes estimate. Keep each entry under 25 lines.
- A rehearsal section working three of them through as mini-plans the owner can narrate aloud: cross-source dedupe (stage in the §6 pipeline, key choice, which record wins, the `2 sources` meta item), geo radius (bounding box in SQL, haversine in Go, two new params and validation), sort options (one change in domain ordering, a select in the status line per BRANDING §5.7's precedent).
- A short "what I would say" paragraph for the two trade-offs most likely to be questioned: scoring weights and SQL-versus-Go ranking.

Acceptance:
- Every referenced symbol exists in the code (a reviewer greps each one).
- Plain product voice, no emoji, under 300 lines.

Validation: N/A (documentation). Record a one-line justification with --role validation.
data.title: Extension playbook: how each likely live-session requirement lands (docs/EXTENSIONS.md)

data.description:
Produce the zip the recruiter receives and prove it works from a fresh directory using only the README. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §12; Instructions.pdf ("send us a zip of your project, code plus a short README").

Why: the last mile. The zip must run on a machine that has only Docker, and the README must be sufficient on its own.

Scope:
- `make dist`: builds dist/brillio-listings-YYYYMMDD.zip from a clean tree excluding .git, node_modules, *.db, .lattice, dist, the two handout PDFs, and OS cruft. Prints the size and the file list summary.
- scripts/verify-dist.sh: extracts the zip into a fresh temporary directory, runs `docker compose up -d`, waits for health, runs the smoke checks from BC-13, runs `make check` (natively if Go and Node are present, otherwise inside the containers), tears down, and cleans up. Fails on any emoji codepoint in the extracted tree.
- Fix whatever the fresh-directory run surfaces (a missing file in the zip, a README step that assumes local state, a path that only worked in the original checkout).

Acceptance:
- `make dist` then `scripts/verify-dist.sh dist/<zip>` passes end to end.
- The README in the zip is sufficient: the verifier follows only its commands.
- Zip contains no .lattice, .git, node_modules, databases or PDFs.

Validation: the verify-dist output is the evidence; attach with --role validation along with the zip size.
data.title: Release packaging: make dist zip and fresh-directory verification

data.description: Follow-up from BC-4 code review art_01M4W3X92E3R58R3C7QHCR8TXJ (PASS, two minor findings, deferred so they do not cost a re-review cycle). (1) backend/internal/store/listings.go: write listed_date with l.ListedDate.UTC().Format(domain.DateLayout) so a Listing built with a non-UTC location near midnight cannot store a different calendar date (seed.Load always yields UTC midnight today, matching the domain invariant). (2) backend/internal/store/migrate.go: the applied-migration set is read outside the migration transaction, so two processes bootstrapping the same new DB file race (second fails 'table schema_migrations already exists'); re-check inside the tx or use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / INSERT OR IGNORE for the bookkeeping. v1 runs one API process, so this is theoretical. Small; can ride along with BC-5 if its owner touches the store.
data.title: Store hardening: UTC-normalize ListedDate on write; idempotent schema_migrations bootstrap

data.description: Found in BC-11 plan and code review. BRANDING §3.2 (Button row) and §3.3 give buttons +0.02em tracking, and §2.1 makes oxblood-deep the hover state of anything oxblood; §5.8's Text button row and the demo's .link (the reference implementation) use no tracking and an underline-only hover. BC-11's Pager follows §5.8 + demo (no tracking, underline-only hover, plan resolution 1 on task BC-11); BC-9 (Clear) and BC-10 (Clear filters, Try again) were sent the same recipe via the Orchestrator. Needed: the branding owner picks one rule and edits BRANDING.md via its §9 process (edit, update demo, republish, approval); BC-14 then aligns all text buttons. Not a code bug; no action until the owner decides.
data.title: BRANDING: reconcile text-button tracking and hover color (§3.2/§3.3/§2.1 vs §5.8 and demo .link)

data.description: Found in BC-5 code review (art_01M4W7VYKS1KWBVC8R1NX7T89M, nit 5). httpapi lowercases keyword tokens with Go's Unicode strings.ToLower (backend/internal/httpapi/query.go), but the store's SQL compares against SQLite's ASCII-only lower(description) (backend/internal/store/listings.go:35). Scenario: keyword=École -> token 'école', never matches a description containing 'École'. Seed data is all ASCII, so nothing is observable in v1. Options: ASCII-fold tokens to match SQLite, register a Unicode-aware lower() function, or document as a known limitation (BC-16 extensions doc). Not fixed in BC-5 (BC-4/store territory).
data.title: Keyword match is case-insensitive only for ASCII (Go Unicode ToLower vs SQLite lower())

data.description: From BC-9 code review (art_01M4W8RJEX9PZGNYXK1279SVG3, nit 5): messages revealed by an invalid Enter or a server 400 are linked via aria-describedby but are not in a live region, so a screen-reader user who presses Enter on an invalid bar gets no feedback. SPEC §7.6 does not require it (out of BC-9 scope). Candidate fix: on an invalid submit, move focus to the first invalid field (its aria-describedby message is then read); or a polite live summary. Keep BRANDING §5.2 visuals unchanged.
data.title: FilterBar: announce invalid-submit and server-error feedback to screen readers
